text.paragraph: Periodic adult preventive visit, with advice before a summer visit to his family in India. [S]

Mr. Ramanujan is a 29-year-old mathematician who comes for a preventive visit three weeks after a cold, which settled in four days. He finished treatment for an amebic liver abscess two months ago and has completed six weeks of rifampin for latent tuberculosis infection, with no missed doses and no side effects. He is eating twice a day now, with dal, curd rice and vegetables cooked in batches, and has regained most of the weight he lost. He goes to counseling weekly, calls home each Sunday, and has had a meal most weeks with families from the local Tamil association. He plans to visit his wife and family in South India for six weeks in the summer and asked what he needs before he goes. [S]

Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan updated. HIV and hepatitis C tests at intake were negative, and hepatitis B screening showed no infection and no immunity. Hepatitis A antibody sent today; he is likely immune from childhood, and the vaccine will be given before travel if not. Before his trip: the injectable typhoid vaccine, because the oral live vaccine should not be given with rifampin; food and water precautions; and the malaria risk for his destination to be checked with the travel clinic. Tdap and the first hepatitis B dose given with his agreement. HPV vaccination was discussed, as shared decision-making applies from 27 to 45; he declined. [S]
Second hepatitis B dose in one month or more.
Travel clinic for malaria advice before he goes.
Enough rifampin for the trip, so that the course is completed without a break.
Dentist through the student dental service.
Next preventive visit in one year.

Latent tuberculosis infection on rifampin (Z22.7). Six weeks of four months: no side effects; adherent. Monthly clinical check done today. [S]
Continue rifampin; finish the course during or before the trip.

Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1917-04-20: three months: abscess treatment complete, rifampin month two, blood count, liver tests, vitamins, mood, and plans to visit home. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 15 minutes, with his consent. He wants full treatment of any illness that could be reversed, and wants his family in India told if he is seriously ill. He asked that his religious practices and vegetarian diet be respected if he is ever in hospital, and that was recorded. He named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and chose not to record other treatment preferences today. To be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
